No two consecutive words can share the same first letter. Write a descriptive, fictional, imaginative screenplay of a fish being pulled out of the water by a human and made to stare at the solar eclipse. The fish descends into a lovecraftian monologue about "horrors beyond it's comprehension" and has an existensial crisisassistant
response:
FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

The sun beats down on the sandy shore as a human, JEN (30s), wades into the ocean, her eyes scanning the water for signs of life. Suddenly, she spots a fish, FINLEY (a sleek, silver fish), swimming near the surface. She reaches out a hand, and Finley is sucked into her grasp.

JEN
(excitedly)
Oh, look at you! You're so beautiful!

Finley struggles and squirms in Jen's hand, but she holds tight. Jen pulls Finley out of the water and onto the beach, where Finley lies flailing on the sand.

JEN
(curiously)
What's wrong, little guy? You're not used to being out of the water, are you?

Finley looks up at Jen with a mixture of fear and confusion. Jen holds him up to the sky, and Finley's gaze follows the sun as it begins to darken.

JEN
(amused)
Oh, look! A solar eclipse! Isn't it amazing?

Finley's eyes widen in terror as the sun's corona appears, casting an otherworldly glow over the beach. Finley's body begins to convulse, and he speaks in a voice that's barely audible.

FINLEY
(whispering)
...the void...the abyss...it's coming...it's coming for us all...

Jen looks at Finley in concern, but he continues to speak, his voice growing louder and more frantic.

FINLEY
(urgently)
...the horrors beyond comprehension...the eldritch abominations...they lurk just beyond the veil...waiting to consume us...

Jen's expression changes from concern to confusion as Finley's monologue becomes more and more unhinged.

FINLEY
(desperately)
...I see it...I see the void...it's a vast, endless expanse of nothingness...and we're all just tiny, insignificant specks...fleeting moments of consciousness in an infinite sea of madness...

Jen's eyes dart back and forth, unsure of what to make of Finley's words. She tries to calm him down, but Finley's voice grows louder, more intense.

FINLEY
(terrified)
...the stars are not stars...they're just cold, dead eyes...watching us...waiting for us to succumb to the void...and when we do...when we finally succumb...the abyss will consume us all...

Jen's grip on Finley tightens, but he wriggles free, swimming away from her in a panic. Jen chases after him, but Finley disappears into the waves, leaving Jen standing alone on the beach.

Jen looks up at the sky, where the solar eclipse is now complete. She feels a shiver run down her spine as she realizes that Finley's words have left her with more questions than answers.

JEN
(to herself)
What just happened? What did I just see?

As the sun begins to reappear, Jen looks out at the ocean, wondering if Finley is still out there, swimming in the depths, haunted by the horrors beyond his comprehension.

FADE TO BLACK.

FADE IN:

EXT. OCEAN - DAY

Finley swims through the waves, his body still convulsing from the solar eclipse. He looks up at the surface, where the sun is now shining brightly.

FINLEY
(whispering)
...I'll never be free...the void will always be there...waiting for me...

Finley's voice fades into the distance as he disappears into the depths, lost in a world of madness and terror.

FADE TO BLACK.

FADE IN:

EXT. BEACH - DAY

Jen stands alone on the beach, looking out at the ocean. She takes a deep breath, trying to shake off the feeling of unease that Finley's words have left her with.

JEN
(to herself)
It's just a fish. It's just a solar eclipse.

But as she turns to walk away, she catches a glimpse of something out of the corner of her eye. A shadowy figure, lurking just beneath the surface of the water.

Jen's heart skips a beat as she realizes that the horrors beyond Finley's comprehension may be closer than she thinks.

FADE TO BLACK.

THE END.
